conclusion: Intermittent severe server lag. Baseline cycles around 150–158 ms, but session-takeover burst produced a 7873 ms game cycle, 7685 ms login phase and 8177 ms tick interval. Final rolling average cycle 200.2 ms and interval 334.1 ms.

rootCauseEvidence.finding: Existing-session takeover calls other.save(); no login work budget bounds the newPlayers loop.
Every checkpoint serializes all online players plus pending logout saves, then synchronously upserts them into market.sqlite.
Each logout flush also invokes a whole-world checkpoint.
WAL with synchronous=FULL preserves durable account/GE consistency. Repeated checkpoints multiply work; do not simply remove durability or save only one participant.

recommendedOrder.change: Stagger fleet restarts/reconnects with jitter; stop duplicate client ownership for the same account. The sampled burst replaced 185 distinct accounts once each, so a repeated per-account loop was not demonstrated.

Bound login processing by elapsed time and count per tick; preserve queued arrivals across ticks rather than clearing newPlayers indiscriminately. Deduplicate queued requests per account and explicitly close superseded requests. Validate both reconnect and session takeover.

Redesign/coalesce redundant whole-world checkpoints inside safe synchronous phases. Include pending logout saves, temp-inventory recovery and cross-player trade/GE consistency, and acknowledge persistence only after commit. Add serialization, SQL, commit timings and checkpoint counts before changing this boundary.

Move hiscores SQL and rendering off the game thread, using the existing standalone hiscores service or a worker. Retain/increase bounded caching, use stale-while-revalidate from the worker, and cache rank lookup maps to avoid repeated linear searches.

Benchmark and add hiscore and hiscore_large indexes on (profile,type,level DESC,playtime ASC,account_id) in a controlled migration. An isolated schema query-plan check eliminated the ranked query temporary sort.

Optimize steady clientOut work (roughly 56–65 ms/tick): player visibility/update construction, zone updates and socket sends. WebSocket batching is already deployed. Spectator feed accounted for 4.7–5.3% inclusive busy-JS samples and is a smaller target.

Add p95/p99 tick intervals, event-loop delay, checkpoint and login counts, and separate processInfo/worldfeed phase timings. Current overBudget counts only cycle runtime, missing HTTP/event-loop gaps.

Plan telemetry/database retention and disk capacity: 86% disk used, about 9.7 GiB free; main database about 55.2 GiB. Do not infer that disk size alone caused the sampled stall. Avoid a live full-database VACUUM.

changes: Login admission stops after 10 candidates or a time budget of min(50ms,tickRate/6), with at least one candidate permitted. Pending candidates remain queued; dead queued clients are discarded.
Session takeover finishes admission within its iteration and updates per-IP counts without denying an existing slot at the cap.
Logout removal uses the same count/time budget, retaining loggingOut on deferred accounts; shutdown drains without this budget.
Hiscores ranking indexes on (profile,type,level DESC,playtime,account_id) for SQLite and MySQL, plus cached username-to-rank maps per leaderboard snapshot.
Management tickstats includes pendingLogins. Durable checkpoint boundaries and SQLite FULL synchronization remain unchanged.

limitations: A single synchronous checkpoint is not preemptible and can still exceed a tick budget. The patch prevents hundreds from accumulating inside one session-processing phase.
The login and logout budgets apply independently. A burst queues admissions instead of freezing the world; some clients may need to retry while waiting.
Post-deploy samples are at a recovering player load. They are not a controlled comparison at the pre-deployment 1,333 players.

Tick-work overBudget counts cycle duration only. Wall intervals still occasionally reached 911ms in the final rolling window, even with all work cycles under 300ms. Early restart warm-up included a 3488ms interval; remaining event-loop jitter is not eliminated by these changes.

followupChecks.assessment: Healthy average cadence, all sampled game-work cycles below300ms; occasional827ms wall intervals remain. Synchronous leaderboard refreshes are a suspected jitter source, not causally proven by these aggregates. Client output is the largest steady phase (~38ms), with player/zone updates and socket sends leading fresh CPU profile.
nextSteps: Increase leaderboard cache lifetime from60s to5min if acceptable; move refresh queries to a read worker and serve previous complete snapshot during refresh.
Add randomized delay to fleet restart/relogin batches, retaining single-controller ownership.
Reduce spectator/dashboard update frequency where acceptable, then optimize repeated player/zone update work based on profile.
For higher scale, move durable checkpoint I/O off the tick thread while preserving atomic multi-player recovery boundaries; this needs stronger recovery validation.

changes: Five-minute leaderboard snapshots; dedicated read worker; stale snapshot during refresh/failure; bounded worker timeout/restart.
Remote lite session login jitter0-5s by default, adjustable via LITE_LOGIN_JITTER_MS or options; swarm retry jitter.
One-second shared player-position JSON; map poll750ms->1500ms, hidden-tab pause and nonoverlapping fetches; roster5->10ticks. Per-tick spectator events retained.
Zone membership cached by player zone/origin/plane; already-loaded zones skip processing without tracked changes.

limitations: Leaderboard snapshots can be five minutes old; stale snapshots remain available during refresh failures.
